_comment: R5-G18-1 catalog #2: the untrusted-email HTML sanitizer (sak::sanitizeEmailBodyHtml + emailResourceIsAllowed in include/sak/email_html_sanitizer.h). This is the XSS / local-file-disclosure boundary for attacker-authored message bodies, so a surviving mutant is a real active-content bypass the suite would not catch. Mutants 1-3 pin defenses the header comments claim but no unit test exercised before this slice (the solidus attribute boundary <svg/onload=>, the multi-line <script> body via DotMatchesEverything, and the multi-pass reassembly of <scr<form>ipt>); the tests slashDelimitedEventHandlerIsRemoved / multiLineScriptBlockIsRemoved / reassembledScriptTagIsRemoved were added in the same commit to close them. Run: python scripts/run_mutation_test.py scripts/mutation_catalogs/email_html_sanitizer.json

mutants.why: HTML5 treats '/' as an attribute separator, so <svg/onload=alert(1)> is a live handler with no whitespace before 'on'. Dropping '/' from the boundary lets the solidus form through. slashDelimitedEventHandlerIsRemoved pins it (the hostile-newsletter body only ever uses whitespace-preceded handlers, so this was an untested defense before the slice).

Without DotMatchesEverything the '.' in <script...>.*?</script> cannot cross a newline, so a multi-line script body is not removed (only its bare tags are, by kDangerTags), leaving the script source as visible text. multiLineScriptBlockIsRemoved pins the multi-line body.

A single forward scan is defeatable: stripping <form> from <scr<form>ipt> reassembles <script> that the first pass already walked past. One pass leaves the reassembled tag live. reassembledScriptTagIsRemoved requires >=2 passes.
Dropping the vbscript alternative leaves 'VBScript:evil()' un-neutralized; scriptSchemeUrisAreNeutralized asserts no 'vbscript:' remains.
Without (?!data:) the url() rule also rewrites a self-contained data: URI to 'none', breaking inline images; cssExpressionAndResourceUrlsAreNeutralized asserts the data: url() survives verbatim.

mutants.id: css-url: invert data: lookahead (only data: removed)
mutants.why: Inverting the lookahead removes ONLY data: url() and lets remote/file url() through; the same test asserts bg.png and file:// url() are gone.
Removing iframe from the danger-tag set stops <iframe> being stripped; framingAndLoadingTagsAreRemoved asserts no '<iframe' remains.
For any non-empty body out != previous('') on entry, so 'out == previous' is false and the loop body never runs -- the raw attacker HTML is returned unchanged. Every content assertion fails.
